About the data & tools

ECMWF forecast data

Hourly air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, wind direction, incoming shortwave radiation, and pressure are read from the ECMWF forcing values associated with the selected forecast time. The meteorological wind speed is not the same as the spatial UROCK wind field.

UMEP and spatial modelling

Existing UCY Campus simulations provide the spatial inputs and thermal-comfort products visualized here. The current workflow uses SOLWEIG for mean radiant temperature and UROCK for the local wind field. Wind imagery represents modeled wind speed at 1.5 m; no directional wind particles are inferred from speed-only raster data.

UTCI — Universal Thermal Climate Index

UTCI is a temperature-equivalent index characterizing outdoor thermal stress using meteorological inputs. The UTCI button displays continuous modelled UTCI values (°C); the Thermal Stress button displays categories computed from the same UTCI field.

Displayed warm thresholds, in °C: moderate >26, strong >32, very strong >38, extreme >46. No thermal stress is shown for 9–26 °C. Cold stress is displayed as one aggregated class for <9 °C in the current raster representation.

PET — Physiological Equivalent Temperature

PET is an outdoor thermal-biometeorological index expressed in °C. This view displays continuous PET model output. We do not add PET thermal-stress thresholds because none are documented in the available V6 forecast manifest.

Physiological assumptions pending verification. Exact age, height, weight, activity/metabolic rate, and clothing inputs used by the UTCI/PET calculation scripts have not been established from the available web exporter source. These parameters will be added here only after checking the actual model configuration. The illustrated mockup's demographic values are not authoritative.

V8 experimental effects: Day/night ambience is derived from approximate solar position at UCY Campus and the selected UTC forecast hour. Rain streaks are a decorative cue triggered only if the ECMWF forcing rain field is positive; they do not simulate local rainfall amount, droplet trajectories or spatial distribution. The toggle changes basemap lighting and 3D geometry appearance only; it never recolors UTCI/PET/UROCK overlays.

Point values: The popup samples the same aligned raster cell from the original UTCI, PET and recorded UROCK wind GeoTIFFs. It reports modeled values, not observations. UTCI/PET use the established common display validity mask.

Forecast display uses Europe/Nicosia for local date/time. Forecast files retain UTC timestamps. This V8.1 is an interface preview; it does not change simulation results or model inputs.

Outdoor Thermal Comfort

Understanding Thermal Comfort

Discover how the outdoor environment feels, taking into account temperature, sunlight, humidity and wind.

Feels Like: How warm or cold it feels outdoors, based on the UTCI thermal comfort index.

UTCI: An equivalent temperature that describes how air temperature, humidity, wind and radiation combine to affect thermal stress on the human body.

PET: An equivalent air temperature that describes how the human body experiences outdoor thermal conditions.

Thermal Stress: Shows the level of heat or cold stress, from extreme cold to extreme heat.

Wind: Modelled local wind speed at 1.5 m (m/s).
